title: Predicting Host-Microbe Interactions and Their Effects on Host Cells Using MicrobioLink
author: Gul, Elias, et al.
materials: Timing: 5–10 min(depending on the size of data)

steps.title: Install Cytoscape 3.10.2
steps.instruction: Download and install Cytoscape version 3.10.2 on your system; this will be used later to visualize the host‑microbe interaction networks.

steps.title: Set up computational environment
steps.instruction: Download the MicrobioLink pipeline from its GitHub repository, then install all required software tools and Python packages (e.g., gget, mygene) so that the command‑line scripts can be executed.

substeps.instruction: Clone or download the MicrobioLink repository.
Create and activate a Python virtual environment (optional but recommended).
Install required packages, for example: `pip install gget mygene` (and any other dependencies listed in the pipeline’s requirements file).

steps.title: Run functional enrichment analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the enrichment script with the exact arguments shown below to perform enrichment on the TieDIE‑derived gene list using the Reactome 2022 database.

substeps.instruction: Open a terminal and change to the workflow directory:
- The `--background_gene_list` file must contain the full set of expressed genes (first column) using gene symbols (as specified by `--id_background`).
- The `--sep` argument defines the delimiter used in the background file; here it is a semicolon (`;`).
- Choose `--analysis_level "TieDIE"` to enrich downstream signaling genes; alternatively, `"HMI"` can be used to enrich directly on human proteins targeted by microbes.
- The output image will be saved as a PNG (or other graphic format) at the path given by `--output_image`; the table of results will be saved at `--output_file`.
- The default ranking metric is `combined_score` (natural log of p‑value × z‑score); you may switch to `adj_p` by setting `--ranking "adj_p"`.

- If you encounter the error `AttributeError: partially initialized module 'charset_normalizer' has no attribute 'md__mypyc'`, verify that the `mygene` package is correctly installed (see troubleshooting 6).
- An empty output file usually indicates mismatched identifiers across input files (e.g., missing UniProt IDs); ensure all files use the same identifier type (see troubleshooting 7).

steps.title: Inspect enrichment results
steps.instruction: Open the generated PNG image and CSV file to review the top 20 enriched pathways (combined‑score ranking) and interpret their relevance to the host‑microbe interaction study.

description: The protocol below describes a detailed step-by-step guideline to predict host-microbe protein-protein interactions and analyzes their downstream impact on the host cellular signaling network. Setting up the computational environment is crucial to ensure compatibility and smooth execution of the MicrobioLink pipeline. Proper configuration of hardware, software, and required packages minimizes potential errors during the analysis and optimizes performance, particularly when handling large biological datasets. Further details in the ‘system requirement’ subsection. Additionally, the ‘downloading and installing the pipeline and the required software’ section outlines steps for localizing the pipeline and explain the process for setting up the necessary environment. It also details how to download and install essential software tools.Note: To effectively visualize networks generated by this analysis, ensure that Cytoscape version 3.10.2 is installed on your system. Cytoscape will be used to create interactive graphical representations of host-microbe interaction networks, facilitating interpretation of the results.Note: For general troubleshooting issues related to software or package unavailability, missing parameters, empty output files, or directory errors, please refer to the “troubleshooting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7” section at the end of this protocol. This section provides solutions to common setup and execution problems. All parts of the MicrobioLink pipeline can be run from the terminal with the necessary command-line argument defined by each script. Each parameter is defined with a specific help message, providing users with guidance on the expected format and purpose of the argument. Example usage of each step is shown using files from the provided GitHub repository (“case_study_input/input” and “case_study_output/output” folders), allowing users to follow along with a real use case. The following sections include step-by-step instructions and visual examples
